doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Live television at the Hollywood Palace and Jerry Lewis
summary: He describes poor audio balance at the Hollywood Palace, taped-live shows, and Jerry Lewis's failed live show.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Let’s talk about live T.V. for a moment.

Oh yeah, well I was thinking about the Hollywood Palace. It was actually taped, but I mean whatever they call it, live on tape. Well the Palace in Hollywood, it was an old theater they kind of made over. And I didn’t realize it in those days, I guess I didn’t expect that much, because I’d go home and listen to the show, and oh yeah I can hear myself or whatever. There was a film clip, part of the Nicholas Brothers, a biography of the Nicholas Brothers that they show every once in a while on A&E, and there’s one of the things they did at the Hollywood Palace. And God it sounds like we’re playing in a big gymnasium and the mic is at the other end. It’s like they didn’t even have our mics on. Like the mics were on the stage and we were like back, way off, almost up like where the balcony is, over to the side. That’s where we were with glass all around us. But that’s supposed to be for isolation so when the singer sings on the stage that the band isn’t leaking into the mics. But it was. And it had been leaking into the mic so bad that they turned off our mics. Because that’s what it sounded like. And I couldn’t believe how — and now you see, like shows that are, they’re live on tape, whatever, like the award shows and all that, and they get great balance.
Well things have come a long way. Technology and all that has come a long way.
And the music was always — how is it video-wise? Audio-wise was, nobody thought that was very important. And like we’d be a mile away from the singer and all of that. You

know it’s terrible to try to do something decent. But that’s why we’re there. I finally figured out like they want the best guys there because even under the worst conditions it’ll sound good if you have the best guys.
Do you recall any times when things really fell apart?

No. That’s interesting. Of course it got to be, with tape, at first it was you were live to the east coast. I guess they still do like “The Tonight Show” and all that, it’s live to the east coast, and they make a tape as they’re doing a live show and they play that for the west coast. But it got to be that if there was a goof, it wasn’t live ever, it was just taped. Oh Jerry Lewis, do you remember, he tried to do a live, boy he really wanted to do it live, and that was just before the Hollywood Palace went on. It was the Jerry Lewis Theater originally. And he’s the one that had it all refurbished and put the sign out there and everything. And I don’t know it lasted about eight weeks and it was a big flop. But yeah, he really wanted to do it live. And I don’t remember any big goofs. Well you know they did all those Playhouse 90s and all those things.

People go on the stage every day and do stuff live. But the radio shows though, God those trumpet players in there, boop, you know a high B flat or C, at the very beginning of the show, there’s the red light and boom, you know, and you never hear any big flubs. You think God, how can they do that? But I’m telling everything. Are you going to edit?
